title: SQLCODE — every EXEC SQL writes to it; +100 = no data, negative = error, 0 = success
sourceContent:
IDENTIFICATION DIVISION.
       PROGRAM-ID. SQLCODE-BRANCH.
       DATA DIVISION.
       WORKING-STORAGE SECTION.
       01  SQLCODE   PIC S9(9) COMP.
       01  WS-AMT    PIC S9(7)V99 COMP-3.
      *> SQLCODE semantics:
      *>   0     -> success
      *>   +100  -> no row found
      *>   -803  -> duplicate key
      *>   -911  -> deadlock
      *>   other -> generic error
      *> Programs branch on these. The Java JDBC equivalent throws
      *> SQLException with vendor-specific codes -- the mapping is
      *> not 1:1.
       PROCEDURE DIVISION.
       MAIN.
           EXEC SQL SELECT BALANCE INTO :WS-AMT FROM ACCOUNTS
              WHERE ACCT_ID = '1' END-EXEC.
           IF SQLCODE = 100 DISPLAY "missing"
           ELSE IF SQLCODE < 0 DISPLAY "error " SQLCODE
           END-IF.
notes: SQLCODE checks are everywhere in EXEC SQL programs. The Java JDBC SQLException model is exception-based, not return-code-based. The spec must enumerate every SQLCODE check so the rewrite preserves the branching.
